title: TableMaster: A Recipe to Advance Table Understanding with Language Models
claim: Structured data traits cause distinct failure modes, and each is addressed by a matched targeted fix that together form one unified recipe.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, four aligned rows pairing each challenge with its solution
description: The figure has three zones. On the left, a table icon branches through a bracket into four data characteristics (Structured, Intensive, Concise, Numerical), each with a colored icon. Gray crossing lines labeled 'Potential Causes' link these to the middle column. The middle column, 'Challenges', has four gray-boxed rows (C1–C4). Each row is a mini pipeline of table, question, LM logo, and output, ending in a red X that marks a failure such as hallucination, calculation error or logical error. The right column, 'Proposed Solutions', has four matching rows (S1–S4) with the same layout, but each adds a fix step such as a focused table, verbalization, program-aided reasoning or normalization. These rows end in green check marks. The red-versus-green contrast draws the eye first.
caption: Overview of the challenges and proposed solutions in this work. Tabular data is inherently structured, dense, concise, and numerical. Based on these characteristics, we identify four key challenges. To address them, we propose four targeted solutions. The gray arrows between the characteristics and challenges represent the potential causes of these challenges stemming from specific characteristics. Each proposed solution corresponds to the challenge presented on the left in the same row. TableMaster is a unified recipe developed based on these findings.
abstract: Tables serve as a fundamental format for representing structured relational data. While current language models (LMs) excel at many text-based tasks, they still face challenges in table understanding due to the complex characteristics of tabular data, such as their structured nature. In this paper, we aim to enhance LMs for improved table understanding. We identify four key challenges: 1) difficulty in locating target data, 2) deficiency in table semantics, 3) numerical inaccuracies in textual reasoning, and 4) semantic inflexibility in symbolic reasoning. To address these issues, we propose TableMaster, a recipe and comprehensive framework that integrates multiple solutions to overcome these obstacles. TableMaster first extracts relevant table content and verbalizes it with enriched semantic context. Additionally, we introduce adaptive reasoning, a flexible approach that dynamically adjusts between textual and symbolic reasoning, tailoring the reasoning process to each query. Extensive analyses and experiments demonstrate our findings and the effectiveness of TableMaster. On the WikiTQ dataset, TableMaster achieves an accuracy of 78.13% using GPT-4o-mini, surpassing existing baselines. We hope this work will serve as a practical step toward more robust and reliable table understanding.
